text: Under the Curry–Howard correspondence, a proof of a proposition P corresponds to:
choices: a truth-table row that makes P true
a model in which P holds
explanation: Curry–Howard identifies propositions with types and proofs with terms/programs: a proof of P is a term t : P, and type-checking is proof verification. Option B is a semantic (truth-table) notion, option D is model-theoretic, and option C is Gödel numbering — none is the proofs-as-programs identification.
